title: Bridge Call: COO, Joliet Stops Shipping

callee.name: Crisis Management Team Bridge
callee.label: CMT bridge: CEO, BCM, CFO on the line

transcript.speaker: COO
transcript.text: It's the COO. Can everyone hear me? Okay. Joliet just stopped shipping. As of 15:30, nothing is going out the door.

transcript.speaker: COO
transcript.text: The warehouse system is offline. The label printers have nothing to print. The carrier pickups at 16:00 and 17:30 are going to leave empty. That's a normal day, 4,100 parts orders, and right now we can't ship a single one.

transcript.speaker: COO
transcript.text: The dealer portal shows a blank page. No order status, no parts lookup. Dealers are going to start calling, if they haven't already.

transcript.speaker: COO
transcript.text: On the plants. Rockford, Beloit and Dubuque are running the controllers in manual mode, so the lines can physically run. But we have no work orders and no lot tracking. Whatever we build tonight, we can't trace.

transcript.speaker: COO
transcript.text: And Fieldmark's buyer has already called Rockford twice. The plant manager didn't tell him anything, but he won't hold him off much longer.

transcript.speaker: COO
transcript.text: So I need an answer. My plant managers want to know, do we keep building blind through second shift, or do we stop the lines? And who's taking Fieldmark's call?

voiceStyles.COO: Man in his 50s, operations veteran, clipped and urgent, talking fast while walking; controlled frustration, not panic

instructorNote: This call makes the operating impact real and starts the recovery clocks. Watch for the BCM to start the Joliet clock at 15:30 against a 24-hour RTO with a 60 percent floor (about 2,460 orders a day). The BCM should also start the dealer portal clock (24-hour RTO) and count the 5 days of finished goods against customers' inventory of under 10 days. The COO owns any line-stop decision, and anything over 24 hours goes to the CEO. The CFO should frame an impact range of about 8.5 million dollars in sales per lost day, and Fieldmark and other customer calls should go to the CMT under ICMP 7 instead of plant staff answering them.
